clue.text: Arouse hostility against one possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the words against one may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Someone might well provoke enmity in a particular person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' tells you to rearrange AGAINST ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To antagonise someone is to provoke their enmity or opposition.

clue.text: Grey will have a fling

parts.note: a shy is a throw, as at a coconut shy, so a fling

explanation.surface: Someone grey-haired is going to try something new.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground game in which you throw balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ashy has the pale colour of ash, a shade of grey.

clue.text: Being indulgent to poor cleaner

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of cleaner are in bad shape and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An employer showing leniency towards a cleaner who does badly.
explanation.walkthrough: TO is kept as written, then 'poor' tells you to rearrange CLEANER into LERANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is the quality of putting up with things, a leniency or forbearance.

clue.text: Gets proceeds after a smashing start!

explanation.surface: A thief collects the loot once the window is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading alludes to a smash-and-grab raid: after the smashing, the thief seizes the goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab is to seize or obtain something; in a smash-and-grab the robber snatches goods after breaking glass.

clue.text: Unskilled, yet quite outstanding

explanation.surface: Someone lacking expertise who nevertheless stands out remarkably.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, NOT ABLE means lacking skill; as one word it means remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not able lacks competence, while a notable thing is remarkable and worthy of attention.

clue.text: Disparaging car — it is in need of overhaul

indicators.note: something needing an overhaul must be taken apart and rebuilt, so the letters of car it is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a car that needs a full service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in need of overhaul' tells you to rearrange CAR IT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiric writing mocks and ridicules its targets, so it belittles them.

clue.text: Put out in small boat

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

explanation.surface: Someone sent away in a little vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' suggests banishment, but here it means extinguishing a cigarette by pressing it down.
explanation.definitionFit: To stub out a cigarette is to extinguish it by crushing the lit end.

clue.text: Charge the man going after a bird

indicators.note: going after says the man's pronoun follows the bird in the answer

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A fee levied on a man who chases a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a levy of one tenth of produce paid to the church, a kind of tax.

clue.text: A dolphin has the courage to investigate

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
to nose about is to pry or investigate

explanation.surface: A dolphin is brave enough to explore.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTLE for courage is informal British usage, as in 'lose your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottlenose is a common species of dolphin with a short beak.

clue.text: Showing off snake wound

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
a sting is a wound from an insect or similar

explanation.surface: Someone flaunting a snake that has coiled itself up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as coiled (rhyming with sound), but it is the noun meaning an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Boasting is bragging about oneself, a form of showing off.

clue.text: Henry is to a certain degree game

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
MA, Master of Arts, is a particular academic degree

explanation.surface: Henry is fairly game for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a certain degree' reads as 'somewhat', but 'a certain degree' is the MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Halma is a board game in which pieces jump across a square board.

clue.text: Striking parity?

parts.note: evenness in hitting: returning a blow for a blow, the principle of equal retaliation

explanation.surface: A question about equality in blows, or in industrial strike action.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes retaliating in kind, matching each blow with an equal one.

clue.text: Bothered by ban on the bicycle

parts.note: someone bothered or annoyed is cross
to bar is to ban or prohibit

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by a prohibition on cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes where the answer is found: the horizontal tube of a bicycle frame.
explanation.definitionFit: On a man's bike frame, the top tube running from saddle to handlebars is called this.

clue.text: Enlarge a quarter before spring

indicators.note: before places the compass point ahead of the spring in the answer

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
a well is a spring or source of water

explanation.surface: Expand by a quarter ahead of springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season, but it is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to grow larger or expand.

clue.text: Look like going round for get together again

indicators.note: going round says the first word encircles the second

parts.note: to resemble something is to look like it
as can mean for, as in 'serve as' or 'serve for'

explanation.surface: Seeming similar when coming round to meet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts AS inside RESEMBLE, after its RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassemble is to gather again after dispersing, or to put back together.

clue.text: Honour among gentlemen — no blessing for some

indicators.note: among says the answer sits within the words that follow it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being made a peer is no gift among gentlemen, for some.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Honour among' as the definition and 'some' as the signal; 'among' is the signal and 'Honour' alone the verb defined, with 'for some' finishing the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility, conferring an honour on them.

clue.text: Ask inside, being a novice

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly
inner means inside or interior

explanation.surface: A newcomer asking to be let in.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner is someone just starting out, a learner.

clue.text: Many skirt the issue, but blush

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
to skirt is to edge, and a rim is an edge
issue means offspring, and a son is one

explanation.surface: Lots of people avoid the subject but go red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirt the issue' looks like evasion; each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep red, the colour of a face when someone reddens with embarrassment.

clue.text: Says plainly time's incorrect

parts.note: a spell is a period of time, and the 's is kept as S
out means wrong, as in a calculation that is out

explanation.surface: Someone states frankly that the time shown is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell out something is to explain it explicitly and clearly.

clue.text: Destroys sound vehicles that skid

indicators.note: sound says the word for destroys is heard, not seen, giving the spelling of a vehicle

parts.note: to slay is to kill or destroy

explanation.surface: Something wrecks sound vehicles that slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning in good condition; it is the homophone signal. Sleighs slide on runners over snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleighs are sledges that run on runners, sliding over snow.

clue.text: Check holding of French collegian

indicators.note: holding says the first word contains the second

parts.note: to stunt growth is to check it
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A college student kept in check by French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts DE inside STUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A collegian is a member of a college, typically someone studying there.

clue.text: A beastly female sets rig to rights

indicators.note: putting things to rights means rearranging them properly, so the letters of sets rig are reordered

explanation.surface: A fierce woman sorts out the rigging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rights' tells you to rearrange SETS RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigress is a female tiger, a wild animal, hence a beastly female.

clue.text: See star forming a part of a mosaic

indicators.note: forming suggests the letters of see star are shaped into something new

explanation.surface: Look at a star taking shape in a mosaic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forming' tells you to rearrange SEE STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles of glass or stone set into a mosaic.

clue.text: Returning thanks in the evening, having enjoyed dinner?

indicators.note: in says the reversed word for thanks sits inside the poetic word for evening

parts.note: e'en is a poetic contraction of evening

indicators.note: returning means the word for thanks is read backwards

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Saying grace in the evening after a good meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns TA into AT, and 'in' puts it inside E'EN. 'Returning thanks' suggests saying grace.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been consumed at a meal has been put away; the question mark flags the indirect definition.

clue.text: A slovenly girl brought up in Oklahoma

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: slut originally meant a slovenly, untidy woman

explanation.surface: An untidy girl raised in Oklahoma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses A SLUT. The definition names where the city is rather than what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is the second-largest city in the US state of Oklahoma.

clue.text: Trouble the united nations get resolved

parts.note: UN is the abbreviation for the United Nations
to settle a dispute is to get it resolved

explanation.surface: The UN's problems are sorted out.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle is to disturb or make someone uneasy.

clue.text: Object when spare key is demanded

parts.note: spare can mean lean, so thin
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone protests when asked for an extra key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb, to protest; it is the noun. 'spare key' reads as a duplicate key.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any physical item, an article or entity.

clue.text: Way-out article on farce the church omitted

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: omitted tells you to remove letters for the church from the word farce

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: An eccentric piece about a farce with the church left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitted' removes CE from FARCE, leaving FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at a great distance, far away.

clue.text: A garden feature for the far-seeing

definitions.text: A garden feature for the far-seeing

parts.words: A garden feature for the far-seeing
parts.note: a raised summerhouse or turret built to command a fine distant view, its name meaning beautiful view in Italian

explanation.definitionFit: A belvedere is a structure placed to give a wide view, often in a landscaped park.

clue.text: A player's shot if including no loud music!

indicators.note: including says the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A performer gets a chance if the music is not loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts NO inside IF. An in-off in snooker or billiards is a shot where the ball goes into a pocket off another ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker or billiards, a shot where the cue ball enters a pocket after striking another ball.

clue.text: Forced to turn over a cheese

indicators.note: to turn over means the word for forced is reversed

parts.note: someone forced to do something is made to do it

explanation.surface: Compelled to flip a cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn over' reverses MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a round Dutch cheese with a red wax coating.

clue.text: This grater works better!

indicators.note: works suggests the letters of this grater are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An advertisement claiming this kitchen grater performs better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' tells you to rearrange THIS GRATER. The exclamation mark marks a loose definition: straighter means more honest, so better.
explanation.definitionFit: More honest or upright, hence morally improved in a comparative sense.
